parent_domains.justification: Cyber-physical systems often involve integrating digital algorithms and physical processes, a concept that overlaps with autonomous systems which autonomously execute multiple tasks by integrating control and decision-making mechanisms.
Robotic systems can be considered a subset of cyber-physical systems where the emphasis is on monitoring, computation, and control of the physical processes which are prevalent in robots.
Cyber-physical systems are considered part of intelligent systems since they encompass smart and adaptive systems that are capable of responding to various inputs from the environment.

Networked control systems are a specific type of cyber-physical system that is focused on the control aspect, typically involving the use of sensors, actuators, and networks for communication and control.
Cyber-physical systems often require real-time operations as they need to interact with the real world, executing computation and processes instantaneously to adapt to changing environments.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Autonomous systems closely align with cyber-physical systems since both involve integrating decision-making algorithms with physical processes, embodying automated and self-governing system behaviors.

closest_child_domain.justification: There are no specific child domains related to cyber-physical systems in the given list as all identified domains are general or equally broad.

sibling_domains.justification: Control systems are often part of cyber-physical systems but focus more on the regulation and management of different organization processes, aligning closely with the parent domain of autonomous and networked control systems.
Systems theory provides fundamental concepts that are crucial for understanding the overarching structure and functions within cyber-physical systems.

Real-time systems are related to cyber-physical systems since they often require the integration of computing and physical processes in real-time environments, similar to aspects found in autonomous systems.
Engineering and robotics deal with the application and integration of robotic technologies and engineering principles which are integral to the development of cyber-physical systems.
Multi-agent systems involve multiple interacting intelligent agents, an aspect often mirrored in cyber-physical systems where such dynamics are harnessed to achieve complex tasks.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Control systems are fundamentally embedded within cyber-physical systems as they are crucial for maintaining the stability and efficiency of the systems, similar to how it is maintained within autonomous systems.

unrelated_domains.justification: While cybersecurity is essential to cyber-physical systems, it is not inherently a component or structure that defines cyber-physical systems as a research domain.
Systems biology does not directly relate to cyber-physical systems as it is focused more on biological processes rather than integrating computational processes with physical systems.

Power systems, while they can be a part of cyber-physical systems, focus more on the generation, distribution, and control of electrical power, which is too specific and separate from the general concept of cyber-physical systems.
Energy systems share some overlapping concerns with power systems but are typically focused more on processes involving energy flow rather than digital-physical integrations.
Transport systems relate more to the movement and infrastructure of goods and individuals rather than the integration of computation with physical processes inherent in cyber-physical systems.
Computer networks primarily focus on data exchange and connectivity rather than the seamless integration of computing into physical processes, which is the central idea behind cyber-physical systems.
Smart grids, while they may benefit from cyber-physical systems technology, chiefly deal with electricity supply and not directly the integration of digital computation with physical processes.

While AI system integration can play a role within cyber-physical systems for decision-making, it acts more as a methodology to enhance systems rather than a categorization domain within cyber-physical systems.
Autonomous systems testing, while related to autonomous systems, is a process domain and not directly related to the overarching structure of cyber-physical systems.

Multi-robot systems, while sharing some integration aspects with cyber-physical systems, focus more specifically on coordination and collaboration among robots rather than the broader digital and physical integration within various systems.
